record_identity.title: Account Enforcement Must Preserve Continuity and Contestability

report_title: Account Enforcement Must Preserve Continuity and Contestability
case_descriptor: Lessons from multi-vendor account restriction, false-positive enforcement, and continuity loss
summary: Platforms may legitimately restrict unsafe, fraudulent, compromised, or policy-violating use, but enforcement must distinguish account, organisation, resource, identity, payment, security, and continuity states. A narrow signal should not silently become an account-wide or organisation-wide loss of unrelated records, evidence, billing access, export, recovery, or meaningful appeal.
what_happened: On 17 April 2026, Belo publicly reported an Anthropic organisation-wide Claude suspension affecting more than 60 accounts; access was restored after approximately 15 hours and the cause was characterised as a likely automated false positive.
OpenAI status reporting separately documented incorrect account suspensions, access restoration, and subscription or credit impacts.
These events showed that account-enforcement errors can interrupt organisation-wide work and continuity-bearing access beyond the narrow activity that triggered review.
abstracted_learning: Enforcement legitimacy depends on scope distinction, evidence preservation, contestability, and continuity-safe degradation. Systems must separate suspected abuse from confirmed abuse, implicated activity from unrelated records, active execution from read or export access, and temporary containment from terminal account loss.
must_not_be_forgotten: A security or abuse signal is not automatically a final account-wide determination.
Shared, pooled, delegated, family, team, organisation, and compromised-account states require distinct classification.
Active generation or execution may be restricted without unnecessarily removing read, export, billing, appeal, or recovery access.
The scope, reason, confidence, duration, review pathway, and restoration condition of a restriction should be legible.
Organisation-wide blast radius requires heightened review and continuity safeguards.
Not every ban is erroneous, and not every multi-account or shared-resource pattern is legitimate.
generalisation_boundary: This lesson does not prevent immediate restriction where security, safety, fraud, legal, or abuse risks justify containment, and it does not presume that public user reports establish platform fault. It applies where enforcement scope, state classification, continuity access, evidence, review, or restoration is disproportionate or insufficiently legible.
